FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
Four-way stop and uncontrolled intersection share the same tie-break: when two arrive together, the driver on the left waits for the driver on the right. [A01]
Why it matters: group intersections; difficulty two; confusable sec07-F10 vs sec07-F12. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A01
A green light lets you go but does not give you the right-of-way; anyone already in the intersection still goes first. [A01]
Why it matters: group intersections; difficulty two; prereq sec07-F03 and sec07-F04. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A01
Move-over speed depends on the posted limit: at 45 MPH or below slow to 25 MPH, and above 45 MPH slow to 20 MPH under the limit. [A01]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; difficulty three; prereq sec07-F22. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A01
For an approaching emergency vehicle you pull right and stop, but for one already stopped at the roadside you leave a lane open or slow down as you pass. [A01]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; difficulty two; confusable sec07-F19 vs sec07-F21. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A01
The school bus stop applies in both directions; only a median or other physical barrier between you and the bus excuses you from stopping. [A01]
Why it matters: group school bus; difficulty two; prereq sec07-F26. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A01
On a narrow mountain road the downhill vehicle is the one that normally yields, not the uphill one, unless the uphill vehicle can more practically reach a turnout. [A01]
Why it matters: group special roads; difficulty two; prereq sec07-F18. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A01
A bicyclist on the roadway is treated as a vehicle, but the same rider in a crosswalk or on a sidewalk is treated as a pedestrian. [A01]
Why it matters: group vulnerable users; difficulty two; prereq sec07-F08. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A01
Maintenance vehicles use flashing yellow and blue lights, while emergency vehicles may use red, blue, white or yellow lights with a siren or air horn. [A01]
Why it matters: group special vehicles; difficulty two; confusable sec07-F23 vs sec07-F19. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0014]

Misconception: having a green light means you have the right-of-way; the law gives the right-of-way to no one. [A01]
Misconception: you must stop for a school bus only when it is on your side of the road; you stop on either side unless a barrier separates you. [A01]
Misconception: when a siren approaches in an intersection you should stop right there; drive through first and then pull over. [A01]
Misconception: pedestrians will always hear your car; some are deaf, hard of hearing, deaf-blind or blind. [A01]
Mnemonic: Tie at the stop, yield to the right. [A01]
Mnemonic: Downhill backs, uphill climbs. [A01]
Glossary: Right-of-way means the legal duty of one road user to let another go first. [A01]
Glossary: Uncontrolled intersection means an intersection with no stop signs or traffic lights. [A01]
Glossary: Staggered formation means several plows working together offset diagonally from one another, which may not be passed. [A01]
